criteria.criterion: A new fake-host test in gh.rs: the candidate has a failed history job and 'fmt, clippy, tests' in progress then completed; land polls (sleeps) until 'fmt, clippy, tests' completes and only then replaces the early head. Run cargo test -p athena-core and see it pass.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: land_pr_waits_for_the_named_check_run_when_the_history_job_failed passed. Each look in its script includes a failed 'the full history' job. It asserts the log reads check_run, sleep 20, check_run, sleep 20, check_run, replace, and that the note says 'waited 40s' and 'completed'. The old code returned on any failed run, so it would have replaced after one look and this assertion would fail.

criteria.criterion: A new test: 'fmt, clippy, tests' on the candidate is already failed, with the other jobs in any state; land pushes at once with no sleeping and the note says that job failed. Run cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: land_pr_pushes_at_once_when_the_named_check_run_failed passed. It covers the other jobs both in_progress and completed, asserts the log is exactly [check_run early1, replace], and checks the note contains 'fmt, clippy, tests failed'.

criteria.criterion: Existing early-run tests (waits before pushing, pushes at once when completed, pushes anyway on timeout, unreadable or no runs) still pass, and cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check are clean.
criteria.evidence: I ran the land_pr_ tests: all 16 passed, including the adapted tests for waiting, pushing at once when completed, pushing anyway on timeout, and the failure, no-run and unreadable cases. Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy passed, and cargo test --locked passed (1230 tests).

criteria.criterion: wait_for_early_run no longer ends on any failed workflow run; it decides only from the check run named 'fmt, clippy, tests' (a constant), found through the host seam, and its doc comment says so and why (a candidate is not a landing).
criteria.evidence: I read gh.rs lines 2068-2110. The loop calls job.host.check_run(early_head, EARLY_RUN_JOB) and no longer calls ci_runs. EARLY_RUN_JOB is a const set to "fmt, clippy, tests", which matches the job name at .github/workflows/ci.yml:27. The doc comment says only that job decides, because a candidate is not a landing and its other jobs always fail there. The new PrHost::check_run is implemented for GhClient (check-runs endpoint, latest run by id) and for every fake host. parse_check_run has its own unit test.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the changed wait.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff: a new entry under Fixed in the Unreleased section says the wait now looks only at the candidate's `fmt, clippy, tests` check run, explains why, and says the step and the bound are unchanged.

findings.summary: parse_check_run reads only the first 100 check runs of a commit (per_page=100).
findings.evidence: GhClient::check_run asks for commits/{commit}/check-runs?per_page=100 and does not page. This CI has three jobs, so it is fine today.

summary: The change passes. Before the landing push, land now waits only for the candidate's check run named 'fmt, clippy, tests'. The other jobs on a candidate (the full history and the pull request head) always fail, and land now ignores them. That fixes the root cause: the old wait stopped at any failed workflow run. I ran the land_pr_ tests in athena-core and all 16 passed, including the two new ones. The first new test scripts a failed history job and shows land sleeping twice, until 'fmt, clippy, tests' completes, before it replaces the early head. The second shows land pushing at once with no sleep when 'fmt, clippy, tests' itself failed, and the note names that job. The existing early-run tests were adapted and still pass. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test checks passed on this tree. The job name in the new constant matches ci.yml. The changelog entry is present, and only the three expected files changed. One nit: the real host reads at most 100 check runs per commit, which is ample for this CI's three jobs.
